Tune in Sunday night @ 8pm ET/PT for my latest hour-long @CNN special, “The Imperial Presidency” 

From DOGE’s budget-slashing to his attempt to end birthright citizenship, Pres. Trump has waved his presidential pen like a magic wand to usher in major policy changes without Congress weighing in

It’s unprecedented, but it’s also part of a longer political history of US presidents granting themselves more and more authority over the years & decades

I’ll examine that history & share my own though

On GPS, at 10am & 1pm ET Sunday on @CNN …
• Sizing up the most dramatic naval standoff in recent history. I’ll talk strategy & tactics in the Strait of Hormuz w/ retired US Navy Adm. William McRaven—who also discusses his new book, "Duty, Honor, Country & Life: A Tribute to the American Spirit”
• While Ukraine earns plaudits for its drone strategy, Kateryna Bondar of @CSIS tells me Russia has made strides w/ autonomous drones that can strike without human control. As AI reaches the battlefield,

From immigration policy to voting rules, Pres. Trump’s use of executive power has been unprecedented. But expanding presidential authority goes back to the early Cold War & runs squarely through the presidencies of George W. Bush & Barack Obama

At 8pm ET/PT Sunday on @CNN, I’ll examine how we got here in “The Imperial Presidency,” my latest hour-long special

Airing 8pm ET/PT Sunday on @CNN: Pres. Trump has expanded executive power to new extremes. With the stroke of a pen, he has declared major changes to US policy, from citizenship to foreign aid, without Congress weighing in 

Trump isn’t the first US president to take a broad view of his own authority, but this is just what the Founders worried about. In my latest hour-long special, “The Imperial Presidency,” I’ll explain the history of how we got here

How did US presidents get so powerful?

Pres. Trump’s 2nd term is unprecedented for his bold use of executive power—but it’s part of a decades-long trajectory of US presidents expanding their authority, much further than America’s Founders ever intended. At 8pm ET/PT Sunday on @CNN, my latest hourlong special examines the evolution of “The Imperial Presidency”

In the United States, President Trump’s periodic insults hurled toward allies get treated as routine tantrums.  

But in those countries, the accumulation of abuse has reached a tipping point.
